arxiv-1912-01303.title: Predicting Soil pH by Using Nearest Fields
arxiv-1912-01303.creator: Quoc Hung Ngo, Nhien-An Le-Khac, Tahar Kechadi
arxiv-1912-01303.description: Abstract In precision agriculture (PA), soil sampling and testing operation is prior to planting any new crop. It is an expensive operation since there are many soil characteristics to take into account. This paper gives an overview of soil characteristics and their relationships with crop yield and soil profiling.

arxiv-2103-09803.title: Adjacency Graphs of Polyhedral Surfaces
arxiv-2103-09803.creator: Elena Arseneva, Linda Kleist, Boris Klemz, Maarten Löffler, André Schulz, Birgit Vogtenhuber, Alexander Wolff
arxiv-2103-09803.description: Abstract We study whether a given graph can be realized as an adjacency graph of the polygonal cells of a polyhedral surface in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} . We show that every graph is realizable as a polyhedral surface with arbitrary polygonal cells, and that this is not true if we require the cells to be convex.

arxiv-2103-16951.title: Resolvent estimates for time-harmonic Maxwell’s equations in the partially anisotropic case
arxiv-2103-16951.creator: Robert Schippa
arxiv-2103-16951.description: Abstract . We prove resolvent estimates in L p L^{p} -spaces for time-harmonic Maxwell’s equations in two spatial dimensions and in three dimensions in the partially anisotropic case. In the two-dimensional case the estimates are sharp up to endpoints. We consider anisotropic permittivity and permeability, which are both taken to be time-independent and spatially homogeneous.

arxiv-2108-07217.title: On Kostant’s weight q q -multiplicity formula for 𝔰 ​ 𝔭 6 ​ ( ℂ ) \mathfrak{sp}_{6}(\mathbb{C}) Thanks: P. E. Harris was supported by a Karen Uhlenbeck EDGE Fellowship. All authors thank Williams College for research funding support throughout the completion of this project.
arxiv-2108-07217.creator: Pamela E. Harris, Peter Hollander, Daniel C. Qin, Maria Rodriguez-Hertz
arxiv-2108-07217.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pamela E. Harris, Peter Hollander, Daniel C. Qin, Maria Rodriguez-Hertz. Kostant’s weight q q -multiplicity formula is an alternating sum over a finite group known as the Weyl group, whose terms involve the q q -analog of Kostant’s partition function.

arxiv-2110-12119.title: Dynamics Near the Three-Body Libration Points via Koopman Operator Theory
arxiv-2110-12119.creator: Simone Servadio, David Arnas, Richard Linares
arxiv-2110-12119.description: Abstract This paper investigates the application of the Koopman Operator theory to the motion of a satellite about a libration point in the Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem. Recently, the Koopman Operator has emerged as a promising alternative to the geometric perspective for dynamical systems, where the Koopman Operator formulates the analysis and dynamical systems in terms of observables.

arxiv-2204-01317.title: Toric non-Gorenstein loci
arxiv-2204-01317.creator: Kemal Rose
arxiv-2204-01317.description: Abstract We describe the non-Gorenstein loci of normal toric varieties. In the case of Hibi rings, a combinatorial description‘ is provided in terms of the underlying partially ordered set. As a non-toric application we compute the dimensions of the non-Gorenstein loci of the first secant variety of Segre varieties.

arxiv-2309-01443.title: the three hundred : contrasting clusters galaxy density in hydrodynamical and dark matter simulations
arxiv-2309-01443.creator: A. Jiménez Muñoz, J. F. Macías-Pérez, G. Yepes, M. De Petris, A. Ferragamo, W. Cui, J.S. Gómez
arxiv-2309-01443.description: Abstract Cluster number counts at visible and IR wavelengths will be a key cosmological probe in the next decade thanks to the Euclid satellite mission. For this purpose, cluster detection algorithm performance, which at these wavelengths are sensitive to the spatial distribution of the cluster galaxy members and their luminosity function, need to be accurately characterized.

arxiv-2401-01570.title: KEK-CP-0400 B s → K ​ ℓ ​ ν B_{s}\to K\ell\nu form factors from lattice QCD with domain-wall heavy quarks
arxiv-2401-01570.description: Abstract We report on our on-going study of the B s → K ​ ℓ ​ ν B_{s}\to K\ell\nu decay in N f = 2 + 1 N_{f}=2+1 lattice QCD. We employ fully relativistic setup in which the Möbius domain-wall action is used for all quark flavors. The lattice cutoff is a − 1 ∼ 2.5 a^{-1}\sim 2.

arxiv-2409-10428.title: On the number of exact factorization of finite Groups
arxiv-2409-10428.creator: Jesús Alonso Ochoa Arango, María Angélica Umbarila Martín
arxiv-2409-10428.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jesús Alonso Ochoa Arango, María Angélica Umbarila Martín. In this work, we study the function f 2 ​ ( G ) f_{2}(G) that counts the number of exact factorizations of a finite group G G . We compute f 2 ​ ( G ) f_{2}(G) for some well-known families of finite groups and use the results of Wiegold and Williamson [ 26 ] to derive an asymptotic expression for the number of exact factorizations of the alternating group A 2 n A_{2^{n}} .

arxiv-2506-03318.title: Validation of Quantum Elliptic Curve Point Addition Circuits August 8, 2026
arxiv-2506-03318.creator: Francis P. Papa
arxiv-2506-03318.description: Abstract Specific quantum algorithms exist to—in theory—break elliptic curve cryptographic protocols. Implementing these algorithms requires designing quantum circuits that perform elliptic curve arithmetic. To accurately judge a cryptographic protocol’s resistance against future quantum computers, researchers figure out minimal resource-count circuits for performing these operations while still being correct.

arxiv-2507-07218.title: A Study of Non-linear Flows and Shear Banding in Wormlike Micelles Under Varying Elasticity, Flow Curvature, and Surfactant Chemistry
arxiv-2507-07218.creator: Alfredo Scigliani, Hadi Mohammadigoushki
arxiv-2507-07218.description: Abstract We report the flow dynamics of two shear-banding wormlike micellar solutions with distinct surfactant chemistries in a Taylor–Couette (TC) setup following a startup shear. The solutions, formulated with CTAB/NaSal and CPyCl/NaSal, exhibit comparable bulk rheology and equilibrium microstructural properties. By varying the TC gap size, we systematically examine elasticity number over a range of 1.28 × 10 5 1.

arxiv-2602-09409.title: A theoretical one-dimensional model for variable-density Rayleigh–Taylor turbulence
arxiv-2602-09409.creator: Chian Yeh Goh, Guillaume Blanquart
arxiv-2602-09409.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Chian Yeh Goh, Guillaume Blanquart. In an early theoretical work published in 1965, 3 proposed a turbulent diffusivity model for Rayleigh–Taylor (RT) mixing. We review its derivation and present alternative arguments leading to the same final similarity equation. The original work then introduced an approximation that led to a simplified ordinary differential equation (ODE), which was used primarily to derive the important scaling result, h ∼ ( ln ⁡ R ) ​ g ​ t 2 h\sim(\ln R)gt^{2} .

arxiv-2603-24801.title: Dissecting Model Failures in Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Segmentation through Explainability-Driven Analysis
arxiv-2603-24801.creator: Abu Noman Md Sakib, Merjulah Roby, Zijie Zhang, Satish Muluk, Mark K. Eskandari, Ender A. Finol

pmc-10553809.title: Social affective behaviors among female rats involve the basolateral amygdala and insular cortex
pmc-10553809.creator: Anthony Djerdjaj, Nathaniel S. Rieger, Bridget H. Brady, Bridget N. Carey, Alexandra J. Ng, John P. Christianson
pmc-10553809.description: The ability to detect, appraise, and respond to another’s emotional state is essential to social affective behavior. This is mediated by a network of brain regions responsible for integrating external cues with internal states to orchestrate situationally appropriate behavioral responses.

pmc-10587945.title: Patient‐derived organoid culture in epithelial ovarian cancers—Techniques, applications, and future perspectives
pmc-10587945.creator: Wai Sun Chan, Xuetang Mo, Philip Pun Ching Ip, Ka Yu Tse
pmc-10587945.description: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is a heterogeneous disease composed of different cell types with different molecular aberrations. Traditional cell lines and mice models cannot recapitulate the human tumor biology and tumor microenvironment (TME). Patient‐derived organoids (PDOs) are freshly derived from patients' tissues and are then cultured with extracellular matrix and conditioned medium.

pmc-10635909.title: Effects of traditional Chinese culture-based bibliotherapy on the spiritual health of patients with liver cancer
pmc-10635909.creator: Ling Huang, Honghui Zhang, Yuting Xiao, Qian Li, Xiu Huang, Lihui Li, Shan Xiao, Ou Li, Le Wang
pmc-10635909.description: BackgroundLiver cancer is a serious global health problem and is associated with poor spiritual health. Bibliotherapy is beneficial in improving health outcomes in cancer patients, yet there is a lack of empirical evidence of its effect on the spiritual health of liver cancer patients in China.

pmc-11397657.title: Quantification of Airborne Particulate Matter and Trace Element Deposition on Hedera helix and Senecio cineraria Leaves
pmc-11397657.creator: Anabel Saran, Mariano Javier Mendez, Diego Gabriel Much, Valeria Imperato, Sofie Thijs, Jaco Vangronsveld, Luciano Jose Merini
pmc-11397657.description: In both developed and developing countries, atmospheric pollution with particulate matter (PM) remains an important issue. Despite the health effects of poor air quality, studies on air pollution are often limited by the high costs of continuous monitoring and the need for extensive sampling. Furthermore, these particles are often enriched with potentially toxic trace elements and organic pollutants.

pmc-11447073.title: Characteristics and outcomes of atrial fibrillation detected before and after acute ischemic stroke
pmc-11447073.creator: Lucio D’Anna, Michele Romoli, Kirsten Harvey, Eleni Korompoki, Roland Veltkamp
pmc-11447073.description: BackgroundAtrial fibrillation (AF) can be known before the stroke (KAF) or be newly detected after stroke (AFDAS). It is unknown whether the outcome of stroke differs between KAF and AFDAS. We performed a propensity-matched analysis to investigate the outcome of patients with AFDAS and their counterparts with KAF.

pmc-11478592.title: Palladium-Functionalized Polysiloxane Drop-Casted on Carbon Paper as a Heterogeneous Catalyst for the Suzuki–Miyaura Reaction
pmc-11478592.creator: Ekaterina A. Golovenko, Anastasia N. Kocheva, Artem V. Semenov, Svetlana O. Baykova, Konstantin V. Deriabin, Sergey V. Baykov, Vadim P. Boyarskiy, Regina M. Islamova
pmc-11478592.description: In this work, a Pd(II)-C,N-cyclometalated complex was grafted to polysiloxanes via azide–alkyne cycloaddition. The obtained polymer–metal complex (Pd-PDMS) acts as a catalyst in the Suzuki–Miyaura reaction. Pd-PDMS was drop-casted onto a carbon fiber support, and the resulting membrane demonstrated catalytic activity in the cross-coupling reaction without yield loss after several catalytic cycles.

pmc-11586550.title: Two‐dimensional echocardiographic right heart ratios for assessment of right heart size in dogs: Reference intervals and reproducibility
pmc-11586550.creator: Jacqueline N. Sankisov, Lance C. Visser, Kate E. Davis, June A. Boon, Evan S. Ross, Abigail C. Laws
pmc-11586550.description: BackgroundReference intervals for simple body weight‐independent measurements of right heart size and function are limited.ObjectivesGenerate reference intervals for measurements of right heart size indexed to the long‐axis aortic valve diameter (AoD) or corresponding left heart structure (right heart ratios) and describe the reproducibility of these indices.AnimalsNinety healthy adult dogs of variable body weight.MethodsProspective study.

pmc-11595613.title: In Search of the Role of Three-Finger Starfish Proteins
pmc-11595613.creator: Ekaterina N Lyukmanova, Maxim L Bychkov, Andrei M Chernikov, Ilya D Kukushkin, Dmitrii S Kulbatskii, Sergey V Shabelnikov, Mikhail A Shulepko, Ran Zhao, Wenxiao Guo, Mikhail P Kirpichnikov, Zakhar O Shenkarev, Alexander S Paramonov, Steve Peigneur, Azizur Rahman
pmc-11595613.description: Three-finger proteins (TFPs), or Ly6/uPAR proteins, are characterized by the beta-structural LU domain containing three protruding “fingers” and stabilized by four conserved disulfide bonds. TFPs were initially characterized as snake alpha-neurotoxins, but later many studies showed their regulatory roles in different organisms. Despite a known expression of TFPs in vertebrates, they are poorly studied in other taxa.

pmc-11728798.title: Deciphering Surface-Localized Structure of Nanodiamonds
pmc-11728798.creator: Li Ma, Zhijie He, Keyuan Chen, Hanqing Li, Yongzhi Wu, Jueyi Ye, Hongying Hou, Ju Rong, Xiaohua Yu
pmc-11728798.description: Nanomaterials, heralded as the “new materials of the 21st century” for their remarkable physical and chemical properties and broad application potential, have attracted substantial attention in recent years. Among these materials, which challenge traditional physical boundaries, nanodiamonds (NDs) are widely applied across diverse industries due to their exceptional surface multifunctionality and chemical stability.

pmc-12437208.title: Gender Differences in Depressive Symptomatology Among Turkish Immigrants: An Analysis of PHQ9 Scores
pmc-12437208.creator: E. D. Cindik-Herbrueggen
pmc-12437208.description: IntroductionDepression is a pervasive mental health disorder that can significantly influence symptomatology, which remains a crucial area of research. This study aims to investigate whether gender correlates with PHQ-9 total scores, enhancing the general understanding of depression across different demographic groups.

pmc-12504436.title: Programmable afterglow tuning in monodisperse SiO2 microparticles through spatially confined emitter doping
pmc-12504436.creator: Xue Chen, Zhenyu Gong, Chenxi Peng, Tian Bai, Zhongbin Wu, Weidong Xu, Xiaowang Liu, Wei Huang
pmc-12504436.description: Developing monodisperse microparticles with tailored afterglow properties is crucial for optoelectronic applications, achieving afterglow tuning in uniform microsized platforms remains a significant challenge. Here, we present programmable afterglow tuning in monodisperse SiO2 MPs through spatially confined emitter doping, creating core@shell@shell SiO2 MPs. By repeatedly performing pseudomorphic transformation, we achieve spatially confined doping of 4-phenylpyridine, 4,4’-bipyridine, and 1,8-naphthalimide into different layers.

pmc-13081657.title: Clostridium zhoujianii sp. nov., a novel gram-negative species isolated from bat feces and its genetic characteristics
pmc-13081657.creator: Jian Zhou, Tao Gu, Jingzhu Zhou, Xiaoxiao Zeng, Ying Liu, Fengming Chen, Yong Hu, Shijun Li
pmc-13081657.description: A strictly anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterial strain, designated LP20ᵀ, was isolated from the intestinal contents of bats collected in Qiandongnan, China. Phylogenetic analysis of the 16 S rRNA gene revealed that strain LP20ᵀ shared its highest similarity with Clostridium paraputrificum ATCC 25780ᵀ (98.10%), a value below the accepted threshold for species delineation.

pmc-13085279.title: Endoscopic contouring of posterior nasal aperture in children clinical efficacy of multiplanar stenotic OSA: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13085279.creator: Haiyan Deng, Wanting Li, Yanjiao Xu, Yufeng Guo, Xiaohui Wu, Xingqiang Gao
pmc-13085279.description: ObjectiveTo analyze clinical data from 112 pediatric patients with adenoid hypertrophy complicated by posterior septal hypertrophy, inferior turbinate hypertrophy, and eustachian tube hypertrophy, and to evaluate the efficacy and safety of endoscopic posterior nasal aperture contouring surgery for Obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS).
